feedback.problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=10\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{10}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =5 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$
